statement.text:
T1: Sliding puck
A small uniform-density puck of radius \(r\) moves without rotation on a horizontal plane at speed \(v_0\). It meets a fixed semicircular wall of radius \(R\gg r\) and begins moving along the wall. Its coefficient of friction with the wall is \(\mu\). Friction with the horizontal plane is negligible.

a
Find the speed \(v_e\) when the puck leaves the wall.
b
Sketch \(v_e(\mu)\), indicating important features. You are encouraged to sketch it even if you have not found the exact formula.

children.text: a. Sliding followed by possible rolling

The wall normal force supplies centripetal acceleration, \(N=Mv^2/R\), to leading order in \(r/R\). Friction \(F=\mu Mv^2/R\) decreases the translation speed and spins the puck with moment of inertia \(I=Mr^2/2\).

Integration of distance gives \(l=v_0\tau\ln(1+t/\tau)\). At the wall end \(l=\pi R\), so the hypothetical sliding-exit time is \(t_e=\tau(e^{\pi\mu}-1)\). Compare it with \(t_1\):

Using \(dl=R\,d\varphi=v\,dt\), the same equations give \(dv/v=-\mu\,d\varphi\). Hence \(v(\varphi)=v_0e^{-\mu\varphi}\) and \(r\omega=2v_0(1-e^{-\mu\varphi})\). solution.text:
T1: Sliding puck
a. Sliding followed by possible rolling
The wall normal force supplies centripetal acceleration, \(N=Mv^2/R\), to leading order in \(r/R\). Friction \(F=\mu Mv^2/R\) decreases the translation speed and spins the puck with moment of inertia \(I=Mr^2/2\).

\[\dot v=-\frac\mu Rv^2,\qquad r\dot\omega=\frac{2\mu}{R}v^2,\qquad v(0)=v_0,\quad\omega(0)=0.\]
Define \(\tau=R/(\mu v_0)\). Integrating while contact slips gives
\[v(t)=\frac{v_0}{1+t/\tau},\qquad r\omega(t)=\frac{2v_0(t/\tau)}{1+t/\tau}.\]

Rolling begins when \(v=r\omega\), at \(t_1=\tau/2\) and \(v_1=2v_0/3\). No tangential friction is needed afterward, since the normal force acts through the centre. Integration of distance gives \(l=v_0\tau\ln(1+t/\tau)\). At the wall end \(l=\pi R\), so the hypothetical sliding-exit time is \(t_e=\tau(e^{\pi\mu}-1)\). Compare it with \(t_1\):
\[\mu_c=\frac{\ln(3/2)}\pi,\qquad v_e=\begin{cases}v_0e^{-\pi\mu},&0\le\mu\le\mu_c,\\2v_0/3,&\mu\ge\mu_c.\end{cases}\]
Alternative: integrate in turning angle
Using \(dl=R\,d\varphi=v\,dt\), the same equations give \(dv/v=-\mu\,d\varphi\). Hence \(v(\varphi)=v_0e^{-\mu\varphi}\) and \(r\omega=2v_0(1-e^{-\mu\varphi})\). The rolling condition occurs at \(\mu\varphi_c=\ln(3/2)\). Comparing \(\varphi_c\) with \(\pi\) reproduces the two branches. This argument also works for other smooth wall shapes with the same total turning angle, to leading order in puck size.
b. Exit-speed graph

Label the intercept \(v_0\), the threshold \(\ln(3/2)/\pi\), the plateau \(2v_0/3\), and the corner where the slope changes discontinuously.
